claims.text: A tailored refractory-matrix HEA will have higher HER and HOR catalytic activity than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The tailored HEA will have better HER and HOR durability than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
Conventional Pt-based electrocatalysts provide high initial catalytic activity.
Conventional Pt-based electrocatalysts suffer degradation and durability problems under harsh electrochemical conditions.
Ni, Co, or small amounts of Ru can serve as catalytically active additions to an NbMoTaW-based matrix for the proposed reactions.
Composition engineering can tune d-band electronic properties to improve hydrogen-binding kinetics.
A refractory multicomponent matrix can provide robust structural stability.
A 0.5 M H2SO4 electrolyte under cyclic voltammetry and prolonged cycling is representative of electrochemical environments typical for HER and HOR.
Controlled synthesis methods such as sputtering and annealing can produce a uniform nanocrystalline, single-phase or stable-solid-solution HEA microstructure.
A uniform nanocrystalline stable-solid-solution microstructure minimizes phase segregation.
A uniform nanocrystalline stable-solid-solution microstructure minimizes corrosion.
The tailored d-band center of the active elements enhances hydrogen adsorption and desorption.
A refractory HEA matrix improves corrosion resistance.
The refractory matrix mitigates dissolution of catalytically active sites.
The combined electronic and structural effects overcome the activity-durability trade-off associated with conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The proposed HEA will have lower HER and HOR overpotentials than commercial Pt-based systems.
The proposed HEA will have comparable or lower Tafel slopes than commercial Pt-based systems.
The proposed HEA will experience less performance degradation during extensive electrochemical cycling than commercial Pt-based systems.
The anticipated performance advantage applies within moderate temperature and pH ranges typical of fuel-cell or electrolyzer operation.
Significant processing deviations may alter the HEA microstructure and catalytic behavior.
